extracted.intended_audience: law students and patent practitioners (judges, patent attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and principles governing when equity will grant, continue, dissolve, or make final injunctions in patent cases, and related equitable remedies (accounts, inspections, payments into court). Focuses on procedural and substantive criteria for interlocutory and final relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie right by possession and enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the plaintiff has, by proof of possession and enjoyment, made out a prima facie case for an injunction, the court will consider granting relief in equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possession and enjoyment of the patented right creates a prima facie case that can justify an injunction; once made out, the court then considers whether defendant is entitled to further investigation into validity or infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's right to further investigation at law when questions of fact or law exist
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant has a right to a farther investigation into the validity of the patent or into the fact of infringement if he shows there are questions of fact or law which a court of equity does not ordinarily undertake to settle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such questions exist, equity will generally order the matter to be tried in an action at law (or direct an issue out of chancery); the court exercises discretion as to the most convenient and effective tribunal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory nature of injunctions in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: All orders made on applications of this kind are merely interlocutory orders; they do not bind the right between the parties and are 'only until further order'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interlocutory injunction may be granted pending further proceedings and is not a perpetual determination of the parties' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant may answer and displace affidavits; full hearing may change result
rubrics_metrics.description: Even after an interlocutory injunction is granted on affidavits, the defendant may put in an answer and displace affidavits; upon full hearing the law and facts will be reconsidered and the result may differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity's initial order based on affidavits is subject to later rebuttal by pleadings and depositions; courts acknowledge the provisional character of such relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court discretion to send issues to a court of law where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: It is within the court's discretion to direct a trial at law when the nature of the case entitles the defendant to further investigation and the tribunal of law is more proper for consideration of legal questions and fact investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every defendant is entitled to a trial at law as of right; the decision is one of convenience and judicial discretion (many cases direct a law action when complex factual/legal issues exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement (U.S.) to name prior users/places when challenging originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Under our system, if the defendant wishes to try the question of originality in an issue out of chancery, he must set out in his answer the names of places and persons where, and by whom, the invention had previously been used, because the Act of Congress requires notice of these facts in a trial at law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural/specification requirement tied to statutory prerequisites for trials on prior use/originality in the U.S. context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency of action against another is not sufficient to continue an injunction if novelty denied
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact of the pendency of an action against another party has been held not to be a sufficient ground for continuing an injunction where the novelty of the invention was denied in the answer, without putting the plaintiff to bring an action against the new defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere pendency of separate litigation does not automatically preserve an injunction; plaintiffs may be required to pursue the proper defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for dissolving an injunction after trial ordered or pending
rubrics_metrics.description: If a motion to dissolve is made after a trial has been ordered at law, or while an action at law is pending, the decision will be governed by the same principles which governed granting the injunction; the defendant will not succeed merely by filing an answer or affidavits casting doubt if the plaintiff is guilty of no unreasonable delay and adduces auxiliary evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts protect plaintiffs who promptly prosecute the merits and present supporting evidence; superficial or technical challenges do not automatically dissolve interim relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of verdict and possibility of new trial on continuance of injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a verdict has been rendered for the plaintiff but a new trial has been or may be moved for, the injunction will not be continued as a matter of course; the court will consider whether there is sufficient doubt and aim to leave parties in a situation producing the least inconvenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity assesses whether the law proceedings are final and whether there's 'sufficient ground of doubt' before continuing or dissolving injunctions post-verdict; practical inconvenience to parties is considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may stand over injunction motions pending outcome of a new trial or motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes the court will direct a motion for an injunction to stand over (defer) until it can be ascertained what the result of an application for a new trial will be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appellate or retrial proceedings are underway, equity may defer interlocutory relief decisions to avoid unnecessary disruption; accounts or conditions may be imposed in the meantime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering defendant to keep an account pending discontinuance/dissolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The court will sometimes direct that the party against whom application is made shall keep an account pending the discontinuance of the injunction, so that if it finally turns out the plaintiff has a right he may receive amends for the injury occasioned by the resistance to his just demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping an account is a protective device for plaintiffs when equity suspends or dissolves an injunction; it preserves a record of profits or use for potential relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity's general approach when new trial is intended or applied for
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new trial has been or is intended to be applied for, a court of equity will generally leave the parties in the situation in which they stood before the trial; if no injunction had been granted the court will not impose one while the plaintiff's right remains doubtful at law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity avoids imposing burdens on defendants where the legal title is unresolved; if the plaintiff had an injunction and then succeeds at law, equity will not dissolve it on mere suggestion of a new trial unless sufficient doubt exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may review regularity of law proceedings/judgment before reviving injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: How far the court will undertake to look into the regularity of a judgment at law, and to determine whether there is probable ground for a writ of error (and therefore suspend the injunction), is a question of discretion; in some jurisdictions the chancellor has inquired into such matters before reviving an injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity may, in exceptional circumstances, examine law-tribunal proceedings to decide whether to revive or continue equitable relief pending appellate remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account of profits as primary equitable remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: An important part of the remedial process in equity is the account of profits made by the defendant; sometimes an account is ordered in lieu of granting or continuing an injunction, and it is always ordered when the injunction is made perpetual unless the amount would be very small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts protect plaintiffs' ability to obtain full justice and prevent defendants from contracting away the subject; accounts may be ordered during pendency of litigation or when injunction would cause irreparable injury to defendant's business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual inspection of works to enable trial evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an action at law is to be tried, the court will order a mutual inspection of the plaintiff's and defendant's works to enable parties to give evidence tending to prove or disprove infringement; inspectors/viewers are appointed and admitted as witnesses on the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspectors are appointed under court direction if parties cannot agree on persons; inspection facilitates accurate factual evidence on infringement issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief when patent validity fully established — account by master and reach of relief
rubrics_metrics.description: When the validity of the patent is fully established, an account will be ordered of all the profits made by the defendant, to be taken by a master; if the patent has expired, the account and injunction will extend to all the articles piratically made during the existence of the patent, though some may remain unsold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final equitable relief can require detailed accounting and may reach goods made during patent term regardless of subsequent sale status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctions should not be dissolved for mere technical/public-officer errors
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction should not be dissolved merely on account of doubts as to the validity of the patent which arise from objections to the technical form or signature of the letters, or other acts or omissions of the public officers, and not from any neglect or wrong of the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doubts arising from clerical or administrative errors by public officials are insufficient to disturb injunctions already granted, especially when dissolution would cause broader harm; equity protects substantive rights against mere formal defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of defendants who used invention under license/permission
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who has had the use of an invention under a contract for an annual rent or other estimated payment may discontinue payment and, if he still uses the invention, be sued for the rent or for infringement; if the defendant is not estopped by contract from denying validity, the plaintiff cannot recover without giving him an opportunity to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity treats defendants who used the invention under license similarly when considering injunctions; where rent is claimed, courts may order payment into court to await the result of an action at law, or require accounts to be kept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable consideration of prior permission, conduct, and expense (estoppel/fairness)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patentee permitted defendants to incur expense in expectation of continued use (e.g., by sending a draft license and allowing payment under it), stopping their works by injunction may be unjust; the court considers estoppel and the equitable circumstances before imposing or maintaining injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity weighs the parties' conduct, prior permissions, and the hardship of stopping operations; where defendants acted under reasonable expectation and expense, courts may refuse or qualify injunctive relief and order accounts or payments instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and patent-substantive requirements for validity and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The judge stated as law on patents: first, that the invention must be novel; secondly, that it must be useful; and thirdly, that the specification must be intelligible. Further, the specification must not attempt to cover more than that which is the proper subject of protection; if a patentee seeks by specification any more than he is strictly entitled to, his patent is rendered ineffectual to that extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For combinations or new methods using previously known materials, the specification must clearly state that protection is sought only for the new combination or application and not claim broader original invention; whether novelty, utility, intelligibility are factual matters for a jury, but overclaiming is a question of law.
